11. Mr. MA Halim, the learned Advocate for the appellant, thereafter contends that the alleged recovery of heroin from the possession of this appellant has not been satisfactorily proved by the prosecution by reliable and sufficient evidence beyond all reasonable doubt and, as such, the conviction of this appellant cannot be sustained and is liable to be set aside. His main grievance is that the PWs, except PW 10, are all Police personnel’s and particularly PWs 1-7 all were the members of the patrol party and naturally they were interested. Of course, out of the PWs 1, 2, 6 and 7 have only come to depose about the alleged recovery of heroin from this appellant and others and the other 3 namely, PWs 3, 4 and 5 were simply tendered. Now, according to the admission of the learned Advocate for the appellants, apart from the interestedness of the PWs there are some material discrepancies also in their depositions and, as such, they were not trustworthy and, as such, should not be relied upon. Further grievance of the learned Advocate for the appellant is that 2 witnesses namely Sekander Ali and Jalal were cited as the seizure-list witnesses in this case in whose presence the alleged heroin was recovered and seized but the prosecution has not been able to produce any of them in Court to depose and in the facts and circumstances of the case these 2 witnesses were very material. Hence it is contended on behalf of the appellant that for non-production of these 2 material witnesses the learned Additional Sessions Judge ought to have drawn adverse presumption against the prosecution case. 

 19. Mr. MA Halim, the learned Advocate for the appellant, as I have already stated has contended that these 2 seizure-list witnesses are very material witnesses and their non-production ought to have given rise to an adverse presumption against the prosecution case and in support of his contention he has cited some decisions reported in 28 DLR 192 SM Farooque alias Syed Farooque vs. State and 16 DLR 223 Ashrafuddin Ahmed vs. The State.
